findings.description: The research scope check compares porcelain status entries rather than file contents. If an App-Zone file was already modified before dispatch, further edits leave the same ` M path` entry and are invisible to this comparison.
findings.failure_mode: A researcher can overwrite an already-dirty application file and write its report, and research-end accepts the ticket because the additional timestamp checks cover only .run and .beads.
findings.suggested_fix: Record content fingerprints before dispatch and compare them afterward for files outside the permitted report path, including files already dirty or untracked.

findings.description: The checkout parser recognizes only literal `git checkout`, although Git global options are supported by the surrounding SP-1 patterns. `git -C . checkout spike/example path/to/file` bypasses this parser; the other checkout pattern requires `--`, which this valid command omits.
findings.failure_mode: The hook allows prototype contents to be copied into the current branch, violating SP-1's explicit prohibition on checkout path copies.
findings.suggested_fix: Recognize Git global options when extracting checkout segments, using the same command-prefix handling as the other SP-1 checks, and cover the no-`--` form with a regression case.

findings.description: The research scope check compares `git status --porcelain` line sets before and after the subagent runs (comm -13 of the two sorted snapshots). A tracked file that is already modified before dispatch produces the identical ` M path` line after any further edit, so edits to already-dirty files are invisible. In a charting session the ledger (grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml) is dirty by construction: `chart-ticket.sh ticket` writes the open row before research-begin ever runs, and a newly created map doc shows as `??` both before and after. The chart-researcher agent has an unrestricted Write tool (agent-types.yaml write_capable: true), and the only enforcement of 'write exactly one file' is this check. A prompt-injected researcher (fetched pages are explicitly untrusted) can rewrite decisions.yaml or the map doc and research-end reports success.
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted research subagent writes decisions into the ledger or map doc; research-end passes; the session treats the ticket as cleanly researched.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot content, not status lines: record `git diff HEAD | sha256sum` plus a hash (or mtime) of every untracked/modified path from the status listing in the marker, and compare after. Alternatively run `find "$ROOT" -newer "$m" -type f -not -path '*/grimoires/loa/research/*' -not -path '*/.git/*'` the way the .run/.beads check already does.

findings.description: `close --consumed-by <cycle>` is the one operation permitted unattended (chart-guard --close-consumed, plan-and-analyze.md tells the agent to run it). It never checks the map's Status. On a map still `charting`, it rejects every open ledger row (`dw reject ... 'map closed: consumed by X'`), closes every open question bead and the epic, and marks the map closed. That is an unattended agent deciding (by rejection) the operator's open decisions, exactly what chart-guard exists to prevent. Only `--reason` gets the interactive check at line 408. A handed-off map has no open rows by construction, so requiring Status handed-off costs nothing.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended /plan-and-analyze (or a mistyped slug) closes a charting map: open decision rows become rejected, question beads close, and the operator's pending questions vanish from the frontier without anyone answering them.
findings.suggested_fix: In the --consumed-by branch require `doc_field Status` == handed-off (and refuse if any row is still open) before any write; keep --reason as the only path that may reject open rows, and it stays interactive-only.

findings.cross_file_justification: op_close (diff) leaves grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md in place; .claude/commands/plan-and-analyze.md line 44 (diff) adds `grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md` as unconditional priority-1 context_files, and the pre-existing priority-2 glob `grimoires/loa/context/*.md` matches it too.
findings.description: Closing a consumed map never removes or retires the hand-off snapshot. The snapshot's first line says 'these decisions are settled; confirm, do not re-ask'. plan-and-analyze.md loads every chart-*.md snapshot as priority-1 context via the context_files glob, independently of the `golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots` selection described in Phase 0 ('Other snapshots are not ingested' is not enforced by the glob). So every later, unrelated PRD cycle ingests the decisions of already-consumed maps as settled constraints, and once two maps have been consumed the multi-map rule sees several snapshots forever (rc 3 interactive prompt every cycle, rc 1 hard stop unattended).
findings.failure_mode: Stale decisions from a closed map are injected as 'settled, do not re-ask' into unrelated future PRDs; unattended planning permanently fails with 'more than one open map' after the second consumed map.
findings.suggested_fix: On close, move the snapshot out of grimoires/loa/context/ (e.g. to grimoires/loa/maps/<slug>.snapshot.md or delete it; the map doc is the tracked record) and make `golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots` cross-check the map doc Status. Narrow the plan-and-analyze context_files entry so only the selected snapshot is ingested.

findings.description: SP-1 explicitly allows `git push [-u] origin spike/x`, but the push regexes never look at the refspec. `git push origin spike/x:main` (or `spike/x:refs/heads/main`, `+spike/x:develop`) lands spike content on the default branch remotely with no merge, no cherry-pick and no PR, which is the exact outcome D-5.4 forbids. The same goes for `git format-patch spike/x | git am` and `git checkout -p spike/x` (interactive patch copy; `-p` is treated as a flag so n stays 1). None are in the documented 'Misses' list.
findings.failure_mode: Spike content reaches main via a push refspec while every SP-1 pattern reports allowed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a push rule: block `git push ... <any>spike/<x>:<dst>` where dst is not itself spike/<same>; add `git am`/`apply` fed by a spike ref and `checkout -p/--patch <spike ref>` to the checkout copy detector; or at least list these in the Misses comment and in the ICE equivalents.

findings.description: The path-copy detector counts every token that does not start with `-` as an operand. Redirections are tokens: `git checkout spike/x >/dev/null`, `git checkout spike/x 2>/dev/null` and `git checkout spike/x 2>` (the `&1` is cut by the segment regex) all yield n=2 with first=spike/x and are blocked. The header lists plain `git checkout spike/x` as allowed; agents routinely append redirections, so the sanctioned switch is blocked in practice.
findings.failure_mode: Legitimate `git checkout spike/<slug> 2>/dev/null` is refused with the SP-1 message; the agent cannot inspect the spike branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip redirection tokens (`[0-9]*[<>]` prefixed and their targets) before counting operands, or count only tokens that do not contain `<`/`>`.

findings.description: The build-path filter drops questions with `(.issue_type // "") != "question"`, while chart-frontier.sh (same PR) reads the type as `.issue_type // .type`, and bead_row in chart-ticket.sh does the same. If a br release emits `type` rather than `issue_type`, the frontier works but get-ready-work silently keeps question beads in the build ready set (fail-open), defeating the D-4.7 'decision tickets are never build work' rule that implement.md and SKILL.md now rely on.
findings.failure_mode: /implement or /run claims and 'implements' a decision ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same accessor everywhere (`(.issue_type // .type // "")`), and add a one-line assertion in the bats fixture that both scripts agree on the field.

findings.description: The label filter does `.labels[] | tostring | select(startswith("decision:"))`. create-sprint-task.sh in the same PR documents that older br releases emit labels as `{name}` objects and handles both forms; here an object label stringifies to `{"name":"decision:x"}`, never starts with `decision:`, and the ticket is dropped. With such a br the frontier is always empty and /chart reports nothing to work.
findings.failure_mode: Every charted ticket disappears from the frontier on a br that emits object labels.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the create-sprint-task normalisation: `(.labels // [])[] | if type == "object" then (.name // "") else tostring end`.

findings.description: The probe's only verdict is `git status` equality of the main tree. The throwaway worktree shares the repository's .git, so a probe can `git branch -f`, `git update-ref`, `git tag`, `git config`, or `git push` from inside the worktree without changing main's status. Writes inside an already-listed ignored directory (`!! .run/` style entries under --ignored=matching) and edits to already-modified tracked files are equally invisible (same model as DISS-001). The header claims the helper 'exits 1 when the main tree changed'; refs and config are part of that tree.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock probe rewrites branches, tags or config in the shared .git and the helper exits 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot `git for-each-ref` and a hash of .git/config alongside the status, and compare; consider cloning (`git clone --shared`/`--local`) instead of a worktree so refs are not shared, and hash dirty files as in DISS-001.

findings.description: The awk allow-list accepts any new or changed path under grimoires/loa/research/, not the single report path the agent prompt mandates. The subagent may overwrite another map's or ticket's report (tracked files, shown as ` M`), or create `.chart-<slug>-<other>.dispatch` markers, which both count toward the 5-dispatch cap and let a later research-end for that ticket pass without a real dispatch.
findings.failure_mode: One research dispatch silently clobbers other reports or forges dispatch markers; research-end passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow exactly `grimoires/loa/research/chart-${SLUG}-${TICKET}.md`; treat any other path under research/ as a scope failure.

findings.description: The header promises a re-run 'creates only what is missing', but `epic` has no lookup: if `br create` succeeds and the map-doc write fails (mkdir or mktemp under grimoires/loa/maps, disk, permissions), the next run finds no doc and creates a second `Map:` epic with the same `--slug map-<slug>`. The ticket/bead steps do look up by source/external_ref; the epic step is the one write-order step without a reconciliation path.
findings.failure_mode: Duplicate map epics on beads after a transient failure; the doc points at one, tickets may land under the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Before `br create`, search `beads_all` for an open epic with label `map` and slug `map-${SLUG}` (or title `Map: <title>`) and reuse its id; only create when none exists.
